Title: SONAM alumni lead the fight against cancer
NewsSubTitle: The launch of the Machakos Cancer Care and Research Centre
NewsSummary: Governor Dr Alfred Mutua inaugurated the Machakos Cancer Care and Research Centre.
NewsContent:
On August 29, Governor Dr Alfred Mutua launched the Machakos Cancer Care and Research Centre. Alumnae of Aga Khan University's School of Nursing and Midwifery (AKU-SONAM) were part of the team that set up the Centre. They include: Faith Mutisya, Chief Nursing Officer, Machakos County, Stacy Kendi, Julianna Kitata, Ruth Muthuku and Ann Mutisya.

The Centre is the very first to be set up by a county government in Kenya, and will provide free cancer screening, diagnosis, counselling, chemotherapy treatment and management. However, this is only applicable to Machakos residents who are registered under the Universal Health Coverage program. Residents of neighbouring Kitui and Makueni counties will receive the same services at a special rate, while other citizens from different parts of the country will receive the services at a subsidized rate.

Over the past few years, AKU-SONAM Kenya has trained several oncology nurses in order to increase the number of cancer specialists in different parts of the country. While Stacy Kendi was completing her diploma in February 2018, she was also in the process of supporting the formation of the first Cancer Care Unit at Machakos Level 5 Hospital. Her concern was that "the residents of Machakos County have to travel all the way to Nairobi for cancer care, where most of them are added to long waiting lists to see a specialist or get crucial treatments like chemotherapy and radiotherapy." However, her relationship with the Machakos County Government had been in existence before this. The First Lady of the County had helped to organize her sponsorship to pursue the diploma at AKU-SONAM. By the time Stacy was graduating, the county government was in the final stages of developing a cancer registry to ensure that those suffering from the illness had been identified for treatment. Stacy, Faith (another AKU-SONAM alumna) and their colleagues took up the work from this point, screening residents daily from December 2018 to facilitate early detection of the disease. Stacy was also in the Oncology Committee of Machakos Level 5 Hospital where she was involved in planning for the Centre as well as establishing the standards for the quality of services. Faith on the other hand, was involved in community-based screening to gain an understanding of the situation as experienced by the residents of Machakos.

"The launch of the Cancer Care and Research Centre will go a long way in the fight against cancer. We believe in caring for the mind, body, and spirit of our patients through diagnosis to treatment and beyond," said Faith. The fight against cancer continues.
